 Advocate for the respondent No.1.
 Shri Mukesh Parwal - Public Prosecutor for the respon
 Order

This is application under Section 439(2) of Cr.P.C for cancellation of bail of the respondent No.1,
Abishek who was granted anticipatory bail by order dated 22/5/2024 passed in M.Cr.C No.19845/2024.
The offence against the respondent No.1 was registered at crime No.189/2024 at P.S. - Nanakheda District - Ujjain under Sections 376, 376(2)(N), 294 of IPC.

This Court granted bail to the applicant on the following terms and conditions:-
" A ) That the applicant shall co-operate with the investigation.
B) That the applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
C) That the applicant shall not approach or influence the prosecutrix or her witnesses."

The present application for cancellation of bail is filed mainly on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:433 2 MCRC-28589-2024 ground that after the grant of bail, the applicant threatened the prosecutrix and approached her to give statement in his favour and not to support the prosecution case.
For the same an FIR has been registered in crime No.294/2024 for commission of offence under Section 195-A, 294, 506 of IPC.

Counsel for the respondent No.1 denied the aforesaid allegations and submitted that the aforesaid subsequent FIR has been lodged in order to get the bail order cancelled.
This Court by order dated 22/11/2024 directed that the prosecutrix shall be provided police protection to escort her to the Court for recording of her statement.

Parties submits that the statement of the prosecurtrix has been recorded in the Court and she has supported the prosecution case.
Counsel for the applicant vehemently argued that the bail is liable to be cancelled on the ground of registration of subsequent FIR.
Counsel for the respondent No.1 submitted that mere registration of subsequent FIR would not be sufficient to cancel the bail.

He further submits that since the statement of the prosecutrix has already been recorded in the Court, the allegation of threatening the prosecutrix no longer survives as there is no occasion for the respondent No.1 to approach or influence the applicant/prosecutrix.
He further submits that the respondent No.1 shall not approach or extend threatening either to prosecutrix or her witnesses After hearing learned counsel for the parties

, I deem it expedient to not to address on the merits of the case for cancellation of bail since the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:433 3 MCRC-28589-2024 statement of prosecutrix has already been recorded.

However, liberty is granted to the applicant to approach this Court in case if the respondent No.1 again approaches her or prosecturix witnesses With the aforesaid, present application is disposed off.
(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) JUDGE PK Victim X vs Abishek on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85820165/
